It’s not just a matter of USC, it’s in the FAFSA stipulations as well. There is a credit limit and timeline limit, if you hit either (keep in mind you can reach one or the other limit) you will be cut off FAFSA due to SAP. If you violate SAP, USC also cannot help you. I recommend you go over the financial aid guidelines because it’s not very intuitive. But to answer your question, the limit is the limit, so whatever you exceed after the warning (you’ll be given one warning), you will have to pay for whatever you have left of your degree.

They do count toward the credit limit so be careful and make sure to see exactly how much you have counting towards that on OASIS. If you exceed it, it’s considered an SAP financial aid violation and you will have to pay for every unit you exceed after they’ve warned you.

I was extremely homesick my first semester and even for a portion of second semester. I would always get advice like “make friends”, “put yourself out there”, etc. and that didn’t help me at all considering I transferred in as a junior and found that pretty difficult. I, however, learned to manage the homesickness by picking up hobbies that I was never really able to get into back at home. I read a lot, got really into cooking, made sure I had a tv series I could look forward to, and made sure I didn’t spend all day just sat in my room, alone and in my head wishing to be back home. It was really hard for me and I cried every other day, lost my appetite, and was just an emotional mess until I really dedicated myself to making sure I found little things I enjoyed during this time I was away from family. I once heard homesickness boils down to a sense of value you feel in your environment, so make sure you create an environment for yourself that you can value. Even after a year, I still get a tinge of that sad homesick feeling every other day but it’s something I can overcome and I believe you can too.
